question: Do published Kamil white-glass data already contain a coupled signature compatible with pre-impact Egyptian gold plus pyramid-like construction material?

gold_branch: Ag and Cu compatible with an Au-Ag-Cu Egyptian gold/electrum class
matrix_branch: carbonate_or_mortar_vector: Ca plus S and/or Mg distinctly above local Kamil quartzarenite baseline
granite_vector: Al plus K plus Na plus Si with accessory Ti/Zr/Ba/Sr where available
same micro-domain as candidate gold signal preferred
frozen_candidate_rule.coupled_candidate_requires: gold_branch AND matrix_branch in the same sample or spatially linked micro-domain; bulk chemistry alone is insufficient for worked-object status

published_kamil_baseline.source: Fazio et al. 2016, Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 180:33-50, Tables 1 and 3

white_glass_with_dark_coating_L03.interpretation: elevated Fe-Ni-Co relative to clean white glass is consistent with dark-glass coating contamination

white_glass_with_dark_coating_L08.interpretation: elevated Fe-Ni-Co relative to clean white glass is consistent with dark-glass coating contamination

dark_glass_L06.interpretation: strong projectile-rich control; not suitable as primary pre-impact-gold discriminator

morphology_screen.published_white_glass_description: highly vesicular, almost pure SiO2/lechatelierite; generally clast-poor to clast-free and described as inclusion-free or nearly so, with rare shocked sandstone/quartz relics in some samples
morphology_screen.limitation: published petrography was designed for impact mineralogy, not a blinded archaeological-metal search; absence in descriptions is not a dedicated micro-CT/Au-map null

Khufu_Giza_general.limestone: calcite-dominant, with minor quartz, iron oxides and accessory dolomite/halite
Khufu_Giza_general.mortar: gypsum + anhydrite + calcite, with limestone/dolostone fragments, minor quartz and micas
Khufu_Giza_general.granite: Aswan red granite: alkali feldspar + plagioclase + quartz + biotite + hornblende; accessory Zr/Ba/Sr/Th-bearing phases may occur

Sahure_quantitative_analogue_not_identit.why_used: published whole-rock XRF gives a quantitative pyramid-material control while preserving a firewall that Sahure material is not Khufu and not a hypothetical Kamil structure

GOLD_AU_AG.reason: the key Fazio 2016 bulk table for clean white glass reports Ni/Co/Cu but not Au or Ag; therefore the requested Egyptian Au-Ag-Cu fingerprint cannot yet be tested from these published values

COPPER_ONLY.reason: ppm-level bulk Cu without Au/Ag and without worked morphology is not an Egyptian-gold signature

METEORITIC_CONTAMINATION_CONTROL.reason: clean white M23/L04 have Ni and Co orders of magnitude below dark L06, while coated L03/L08 move toward the projectile-rich direction; this preserves a useful contamination gradient

PYRAMID_CARBONATE_MORTAR_MATRIX.reason: M23/L04 remain approximately 99.4-99.9 wt% SiO2 with CaO only 0.12-0.65 wt%; known pyramid limestone/mortar controls are Ca-rich and mortar can be strongly S-rich
PYRAMID_CARBONATE_MORTAR_MATRIX.important_limitation: S is not reported in the Fazio 2016 white-glass bulk table, so gypsum-specific scoring is incomplete

PYRAMID_GRANITE_MATRIX.reason: clean white glass has very low Al2O3, K2O and Na2O and remains nearly pure silica; no published feldspar/biotite/hornblende-style assemblage or worked architectural clast is reported in those samples

MORPHOLOGY.reason: no foil/sheet/wire/seam/solder morphology is reported in the published white-glass petrography

COUPLED_CANDIDATE.reason: gold branch is unscored because Au/Ag are missing, while the bulk matrix and morphology branches do not presently show a pyramid-like anomaly

illustrative_linear_mix_screen.warning: NOT_AN_EXCLUSION_LIMIT. Impact melting, volatilization, phase separation and target heterogeneity violate simple linear mixing. Values are only a screening sanity check.
illustrative_linear_mix_screen.interpretation: under an intentionally naive bulk-mixing model, the clean white samples do not require a multi-percent pyramid-like component; L04 is fit by well below ~1 wt% of the chosen analogue, which is compatible with ordinary target heterogeneity and is not archaeological evidence

priority_samples_for_real_reanalysis.why: clean white glass, 99.9 wt% SiO2, low Ni/Co; best projectile-minimized Au/Ag test
clean pumiceous white lechatelierite, 99.4 wt% SiO2; second independent white-glass target
published as white SiO2-rich impactite with Ni below detection in a later microscopy study; useful independent morphology target
white glass with dark coating; contamination control
white glass with dark coating; contamination control
dark projectile-rich glass; positive meteoritic control

stage_1_non_destructive: micro-CT or high-resolution X-ray tomography for high-density inclusions and foil/sheet-like geometry
micro-XRF elemental maps for Au, Ag, Cu, Ni, Co, Fe plus Ca, S, Al, K and other available matrix markers
stage_2_targeted_microanalysis: SEM-BSE plus EDS/EPMA on any dense inclusion or anomalous micro-domain
LA-ICP-MS or micro-PIXE for Au-Ag-Cu-Pt-Ir-Os-Ru and meteoritic discriminants such as Ni-Co-Ga-Ge where analytically feasible
Raman/XRD/EPMA for carbonate, gypsum/anhydrite, feldspar, mica, amphibole and accessory phases
required_next_measurements.blind_rule: classify micro-domains by chemistry and morphology before revealing whether the host is clean white, coated white, dark glass or target rock

next_gate.name: KAMIL_WHITE_GLASS_AU_AG_MICRODOMAIN_GATE
next_gate.open_condition: obtain published supplementary data or new measurements for Au and Ag in M23/L04/L09 or equivalent clean white glass
next_gate.promotion_condition: Au-rich micro-domain above geological/meteoritic background + Au-Ag-Cu pattern compatible with worked Egyptian gold/electrum + no proportional Ni-Co-Ga-Ge meteoritic signature + independent pyramid-material or worked morphology evidence

sources.citation: Fazio A., D'Orazio M., Cordier C., Folco L. (2016) Target-projectile interaction during impact melting at Kamil Crater, Egypt. Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 180, 33-50.

Hemeda S., Sonbol A. (2020) Sustainability problems of the Giza pyramids. Heritage Science 8:8.
Fahmy A. et al. (2022) Geoenvironmental investigation of Sahure's pyramid, Abusir archeological site, Giza, Egypt. Heritage Science 10:61.
